fr: Les clés sont sur la table.
en: The keys are on the table.
notes: The plural article "les" links to "clés" with a hidden z-sound liaison.

fr: Ils ont un nouveau téléphone.
en: They have a new phone.
notes: "Ils ont" liaises with a z-sound, unlike "il a", so the plural must be heard correctly.

fr: Mes amis cherchent leurs lunettes.
en: My friends are looking for their glasses.
notes: "Mes amis" liaises with a z-sound that marks the plural you cannot skip in writing.

fr: Nous avons un petit sac noir.
en: We have a small black bag.
notes: "Nous avons" liaises with a z-sound linking into "un".

fr: Vous avez un beau parapluie aujourd'hui.
en: You have a beautiful umbrella today.
notes: "Vous avez" liaises with a z-sound between the pronoun and the verb.

fr: Elles ont de nouveaux gants.
en: They have new gloves.
notes: "Elles ont" liaises with a z-sound, distinguishing it by ear from "elle a".

fr: C'est un objet très utile.
en: This is a very useful object.
notes: "C'est un" liaises with a t-sound, and "très utile" liaises with a z-sound.

fr: Ses lunettes sont sur le bureau.
en: Her glasses are on the desk.
notes: "Ses" sounds identical to "ces" and "c'est", so only context tells you which spelling to write.

fr: Où sont mes clés maintenant ?
en: Where are my keys now?
notes: "Où" (where) sounds exactly like "ou" (or), but only one of them takes an accent.

fr: C'est son sac, pas le mien.
en: This is his bag, not mine.
notes: "Son" (his/her) sounds identical to "sont" (are), so listen for the grammar, not just the sound.

fr: Le sac est à Paul.
en: The bag belongs to Paul.
notes: "À" (belongs to) sounds exactly like "a" (has), so the accent must come from grammar, not sound.

fr: Ces outils sont très vieux.
en: These tools are very old.
notes: "Ces" (these) sounds identical to "ses" (his/her), a classic dictée trap.

fr: Tu prends le sac ou la valise ?
en: Are you taking the bag or the suitcase?
ipa: /ty pʁɑ̃ lə sak u la va.liz/
notes: "Ou" (or) sounds exactly like "où" (where), but only "où" takes the accent.

fr: Le stylo est à côté du cahier.
en: The pen is next to the notebook.
ipa: /lə sti.lo ɛ a ko.te dy ka.je/
notes: The "à" in "à côté" sounds identical to "a", so the accent depends on grammar, not sound.

fr: Les valises sont très grandes.
en: The suitcases are very big.
notes: "Grandes" adds a silent -es to agree with the feminine plural "valises", a change you hear only from context.

fr: Mon sac est noir et ma veste est noire.
en: My bag is black and my jacket is black too.
ipa: /mɔ̃ sak ɛ nwaʁ e ma vɛst ɛ nwaʁ/
notes: "Noire" adds a silent -e to agree with the feminine "veste", though it sounds the same as "noir".

fr: Les gants sont trop petits.
en: The gloves are too small.
notes: "Petits" adds a silent -s to agree with the plural "gants".

fr: La montre est très belle.
en: The watch is very beautiful.
notes: "Belle" doubles the letter l and adds -e to agree with the feminine "montre".

fr: Les clés sont vraiment perdues.
en: The keys are really lost.
notes: "Perdues" adds a silent -es to agree with the feminine plural "clés".

fr: Ses lunettes sont toutes neuves.
en: Her glasses are brand new.
notes: "Neuves" and "toutes" both carry silent feminine plural endings that agree with "lunettes".

fr: Le sac est lourd, la valise est lourde aussi.
en: The bag is heavy, the suitcase is heavy too.
ipa: /lə sak ɛ luʁ la va.liz ɛ luʁd o.si/
notes: "Lourde" adds a silent -e to agree with the feminine "valise", unlike the masculine "lourd".

fr: Mon téléphone est dans ma poche.
en: My phone is in my pocket.
notes: The nasal vowels in "mon" and "dans" must not be followed by a pronounced n or m sound.

fr: Son parapluie est vraiment grand.
en: His umbrella is really big.
notes: The nasal vowels in "son" and "grand" sound similar but are spelled with different letters.

fr: Le vent est trop fort pour mon parapluie.
en: The wind is too strong for my umbrella.
ipa: /lə vɑ̃ ɛ tʁo fɔʁ puʁ mɔ̃ pa.ʁa.plɥi/
notes: "Vent" holds a nasal vowel spelled -ent, easy to confuse with the -an or -en spelling families.

fr: J'ai toujours un chargeur blanc.
en: I always have a white charger.
notes: "Un" and "blanc" both carry nasal vowels that sound alike but are spelled differently.

fr: Ton sac est bien rangé.
en: Your bag is well organized.
notes: "Bien" holds a nasal vowel spelled -ien, distinct from the -in or -ain spelling families.

fr: Mes gants sont tout blancs.
en: My gloves are all white.
notes: The nasal vowels in "gants" and "blancs" sound identical despite their different spellings.

fr: Mon sac est très grand.
en: My bag is very big.
notes: The final "d" in "grand" is silent, easy to forget when writing.

fr: J'ai un vieux stylo gris.
en: I have an old grey pen.
notes: The final "s" in "gris" is silent, though the word sounds the same in singular and plural.

fr: Ce parapluie est trop petit.
en: This umbrella is too small.
notes: The final "p" in "trop" and the final "t" in "petit" are both silent.

fr: J'aime beaucoup ce vieux chapeau.
en: I really like this old hat.
notes: The final "p" in "beaucoup" is silent and often mistakenly dropped or misplaced.

fr: Il range ses outils dans le fond du garage.
en: He puts his tools away at the back of the garage.
ipa: /il ʁɑ̃ʒ se zu.ti dɑ̃ lə fɔ̃ dy ga.ʁaʒ/
notes: The final "d" in "fond" is silent, though it resurfaces in related words like "fondamental".

fr: Mon vieux sac est vraiment lourd.
en: My old bag is really heavy.
notes: The final "d" in "lourd" is silent, only heard once a feminine -e is added.

fr: J'achète un nouveau parapluie aujourd'hui.
en: I am buying a new umbrella today.
notes: "Aujourd'hui" starts with a silent h and hides an apostrophe that is easy to misplace.

fr: Mon téléphone reste à l'hôtel.
en: My phone is staying at the hotel.
notes: "Hôtel" has a silent h and a circumflex accent marking a historically dropped letter.

fr: Elle range ses affaires dans l'armoire.
en: She puts her things away in the wardrobe.
notes: "Affaires" doubles the letter f, a common spelling mistake in dictée.

fr: Il oublie souvent ses clés à l'école.
en: He often forgets his keys at school.
ipa: /il u.bli su.vɑ̃ se kle a le.kɔl/
notes: "École" carries an accent grave that changes the vowel and must be written, not just heard.

fr: Ma montre tombe souvent dans l'herbe.
en: My watch often falls in the grass.
notes: "Herbe" starts with a silent h that is never pronounced but always written.

fr: J'ai un joli collier en argent.
en: I have a pretty silver necklace.
notes: "Collier" doubles the letter l, a spelling that cannot be guessed from sound alone.

fr: J'ai un beau sac en cuir.
en: I have a beautiful leather bag.
notes: "Je" elides to "j'ai" before the vowel of "ai".

fr: L'ordinateur est sur le bureau.
en: The computer is on the desk.
notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "ordinateur".

fr: C'est l'appareil photo de mon père.
en: This is my father's camera.
notes: Both "ce" and "le" elide before vowels, giving "c'est l'appareil".

fr: J'aime beaucoup cette vieille montre.
en: I really like this old watch.
notes: "Je" elides to "j'aime" before the vowel of "aime".

fr: L'écharpe de Julie est bleue.
en: Julie's scarf is blue.
notes: "La" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "écharpe".

fr: Elle n'a pas de portable.
en: She does not have a cell phone.
notes: "Ne" elides to "n'" before the vowel of "a".

fr: Le sac de Pierre est petit.
en: Pierre's bag is small.
notes: The final -e of "petit" stays silent, but drop it and the word's meaning changes.

fr: La petite clé ouvre cette porte.
en: The little key opens this door.
notes: The unstressed e in "petite" is barely pronounced but never disappears in writing.

fr: Je cherche une petite montre.
en: I am looking for a small watch.
notes: The e-muet in "je" can almost vanish in fast speech but must still be written.

fr: Ce chargeur ne fonctionne pas.
en: This charger does not work.
notes: The e-muet in "ne" is often dropped in speech but must appear in the written sentence.

fr: Je ne trouve pas mon sac.
en: I cannot find my bag.
notes: Both e-muets in "je" and "ne" can disappear in casual speech but must be written out.

fr: Le sac que tu portes est joli.
en: The bag you are carrying is nice.
ipa: /lə sak kə ty pɔʁt ɛ ʒɔ.li/
notes: The e-muet in "que" is easy to skip when listening but required in the spelling.

fr: La montre qu'elle a perdue était neuve.
en: The watch she lost was new.
ipa: /la mɔ̃tʁ kɛl a pɛʁ.dy e.tɛ nœv/
notes: The past participle "perdue" agrees with the feminine "montre" because the direct object comes before "avoir".

fr: Les clés qu'il a trouvées étaient sous le tapis.
en: The keys he found were under the rug.
ipa: /le kle kil a tʁu.ve e.tɛ su lə ta.pi/
notes: "Trouvées" agrees with the feminine plural "clés" placed before the auxiliary "avoir".

fr: Elle est allée chercher son sac à la gare.
en: She went to get her bag at the station.
ipa: /ɛl ɛt a.le ʃɛʁ.ʃe sɔ̃ sak a la gaʁ/
notes: With "être", the past participle "allée" agrees with the feminine subject "elle".

fr: Ils sont partis sans leurs valises.
en: They left without their suitcases.
notes: With "être", the past participle "partis" agrees with the masculine plural subject "ils".

fr: La valise que j'ai achetée est très lourde.
en: The suitcase I bought is very heavy.
ipa: /la va.liz kə ʒe aʃ.te ɛ tʁɛ luʁd/
notes: "Achetée" agrees with the feminine "valise" because the direct object precedes the auxiliary "avoir".

fr: On a oublié le sac à la gare.
en: We forgot the bag at the station.
ipa: /ɔ̃ na u.bli.je lə sak a la gaʁ/
notes: "A" (has) and "à" (at) sound identical, so the accent depends entirely on grammar.

fr: Ils ont perdu leurs clés dans le taxi.
en: They lost their keys in the taxi.
ipa: /il zɔ̃ pɛʁ.dy lœʁ kle dɑ̃ lə tak.si/
notes: "Ont" (have) sounds exactly like "on" (one/we), a frequent listening trap.

fr: On a mis longtemps à retrouver ce portefeuille.
en: It took us a long time to find this wallet.
ipa: /ɔ̃ na mi lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a ʁə.tʁu.ve sə pɔʁ.tə.fœj/
notes: "On" sounds identical to "ont", so only the surrounding verb form shows which one is correct.

fr: Tu sais où j'ai mis mon chargeur ?
en: Do you know where I put my charger?
ipa: /ty sɛ u ʒe mi mɔ̃ ʃaʁ.ʒœʁ/
notes: "Où" (where) sounds exactly like "ou" (or), but only "où" carries the accent.

fr: Elle cherche son parapluie ou son sac.
en: She is looking for her umbrella or her bag.
ipa: /ɛl ʃɛʁʃ sɔ̃ pa.ʁa.plɥi u sɔ̃ sak/
notes: "Ou" (or) sounds identical to "où" (where), a pair every dictée tests.

fr: Nous avons acheté un nouvel appareil photo.
en: We bought a new camera.
ipa: /nu za.vɔ̃ zaʃ.te œ̃ nu.vɛl a.pa.ʁɛj fɔ.to/
notes: "Nouvel" replaces "nouveau" before a vowel, and "avons" liaises with a z-sound into "acheté".

fr: Elles ont retrouvé leurs affaires perdues.
en: They found their lost belongings.
notes: "Elles ont" liaises with a z-sound, distinguishing the plural from "elle a" by ear alone.

fr: Vous allez oublier vos clés encore une fois.
en: You are going to forget your keys again.
ipa: /vu za.le u.bli.je vo kle ɑ̃.kɔʁ yn fwa/
notes: "Vous allez" liaises with a z-sound linking the pronoun into "allez".

fr: Ils vont acheter un nouveau sac demain.
en: They are going to buy a new bag tomorrow.
ipa: /il vɔ̃t aʃ.te œ̃ nu.vo sak də.mɛ̃/
notes: "Ils vont" liaises with a t-sound before the vowel of "acheter".

fr: Il va ranger ses instruments dans un tiroir.
en: He is going to put his instruments away in a drawer.
ipa: /il va ʁɑ̃.ʒe se zɛ̃s.tʁy.mɑ̃ dɑ̃ zœ̃ ti.ʁwaʁ/
notes: The nasal vowels in "instruments" and "un" sound alike despite their different spellings.

fr: Elle a mis son téléphone dans un tiroir fermé.
en: She put her phone in a closed drawer.
ipa: /ɛl a mi sɔ̃ te.le.fɔn dɑ̃ zœ̃ ti.ʁwaʁ fɛʁ.me/
notes: The nasal vowels in "son" and "un" must be told apart by spelling, not by sound.

fr: Nous allons emprunter ce parapluie demain matin.
en: We are going to borrow this umbrella tomorrow morning.
ipa: /nu za.lɔ̃ ɑ̃.pʁœ̃.te sə pa.ʁa.plɥi də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
notes: "Emprunter" packs two nasal vowels close together, easy to blur when writing.

fr: J'ai rangé mon ordinateur dans un grand sac.
en: I put my computer away in a big bag.
ipa: /ʒe ʁɑ̃.ʒe mɔ̃n ɔʁ.di.na.tœʁ dɑ̃ zœ̃ gʁɑ̃ sak/
notes: The nasal vowels in "mon", "un", and "grand" all sound similar but use different spellings.

fr: Elle a rangé son sac dans le grand placard.
en: She put her bag away in the big cupboard.
ipa: /ɛl a ʁɑ̃.ʒe sɔ̃ sak dɑ̃ lə gʁɑ̃ pla.kaʁ/
notes: The final "d" in "grand" stays silent even though it is always written.

fr: Il a acheté un chargeur pas cher du tout.
en: He bought a very cheap charger.
ipa: /il a aʃ.te œ̃ ʃaʁ.ʒœʁ pa ʃɛʁ dy tu/
notes: The final "t" in "tout" is silent, a common source of missing letters in dictée.

fr: Nous avons cherché ses outils partout dans le garage.
en: We looked for his tools everywhere in the garage.
ipa: /nu za.vɔ̃ ʃɛʁ.ʃe se zu.ti paʁ.tu dɑ̃ lə ga.ʁaʒ/
notes: The final "t" in "partout" is silent, a common dictée slip.

fr: J'ai payé trop cher pour ce sac.
en: I paid too much for this bag.
ipa: /ʒe pe.je tʁo ʃɛʁ puʁ sə sak/
notes: The final "p" in "trop" is silent, easy to forget when spelling the word.

fr: J'ai acheté une nouvelle montre à l'aéroport.
en: I bought a new watch at the airport.
ipa: /ʒe aʃ.te yn nu.vɛl mɔ̃tʁ a la.e.ʁɔ.pɔʁ/
notes: "Aéroport" carries an accent aigu on the first e that must be written even though it is fully pronounced.

fr: Elle a laissé ses clés à l'hôtel ce matin.
en: She left her keys at the hotel this morning.
ipa: /ɛl a le.se se kle a lo.tɛl sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: "Hôtel" has a silent h and a circumflex accent marking a historically missing letter.

fr: Nous avons acheté de nouveaux outils ce matin.
en: We bought new tools this morning.
ipa: /nu za.vɔ̃ zaʃ.te də nu.vo zu.ti sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: The plural ending -eaux in "nouveaux" is silent but cannot be replaced with a simple -s.

fr: J'ai trouvé une clé cassée dans l'herbe.
en: I found a broken key in the grass.
ipa: /ʒe tʁu.ve yn kle ka.se dɑ̃ lɛʁb/
notes: "Cassée" doubles the letter s, and "herbe" begins with a silent h.

fr: J'ai emprunté l'ordinateur de mon frère.
en: I borrowed my brother's computer.
notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "ordinateur".

fr: Elle n'a pas retrouvé son sac.
en: She did not find her bag.
notes: "Ne" elides to "n'" before the vowel of "a".

fr: Il va s'acheter un nouveau portable.
en: He is going to buy himself a new cell phone.
notes: The reflexive "se" elides to "s'" before the vowel of "acheter".

fr: L'appareil photo de Julie est cassé.
en: Julie's camera is broken.
notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "appareil".

fr: Je vais chercher mon petit sac demain.
en: I am going to get my small bag tomorrow.
ipa: /ʒə vɛ ʃɛʁ.ʃe mɔ̃ pə.ti sak də.mɛ̃/
notes: The e-muet in "je" is barely heard but must still appear in writing.

fr: Elle ne retrouve plus sa clé.
en: She can no longer find her key.
notes: The e-muet in "ne" often disappears in fast speech but is required in the spelling.

fr: Nous allons acheter une petite lampe.
en: We are going to buy a small lamp.
notes: The unstressed e in "petite" is barely pronounced but never disappears from the written word.

fr: Il ne sait plus où se trouve son sac.
en: He no longer knows where his bag is.
ipa: /il nə sɛ ply u sə tʁuv sɔ̃ sak/
notes: The e-muets in "ne" and "se" are easy to drop by ear but must be written in full.
